Audio patch disables a recording-start read section; network adds receive-readiness callbacks and early driver attachment; OHCI adds an operational bus-stop PowerOff callback and Genode request processing; shared clipboard conditionally skips a data-event signal, with reference/lifetime concerns documented in the patch. These are source comments/behavior changes, not executed failures or proof all queues, events and external writers drain.

vCPU owns a VM-connection wrapper and halt-event handle, creates the event and switches to hardware at construction. Pause posts an exit signal or marks forced flags; halt waits at least1ms and resets its event, wake signals it. Exit constructs a temporary state reference across an EMT switch then destructs that reference. No explicit derived destructor/release method here closes the halt event or proves VM-session detached/quiescent; member/base/vendor destroy paths remain to trace. This is missing closure, not a demonstrated leak.

Semaphore create/close/signal delegate to IPRT event functions. Multi wait translates milliseconds and indefinite sentinel to relative interruptible flags; relative nanoseconds are converted to milliseconds. Several nanosecond wait variants use STOP, which logs/backtraces then sleeps forever. A supported selected call graph must exclude or control those paths; timeout/resolution constants do not establish cancel/drain/destruction of all workers. No such path was run.

PDM maps known registration symbols to statically linked drivers, with dummy success registrations for some modules; unexpected RC symbol enters a loop and R0 dummy asserts. Driver registry includes disk/SCSI/DVD/network/audio/USB/pipes/TCP/UDP/rawfile/serial/TPM paths. Missing CPU frequency sleeps forever, virtualization selection uses platform ROM, and attempt throws Fatal on failed HRESULT. Registration/status checking does not prove every callback lifetime, actual supported feature path or cleanup.

Runtime composition selects upstream generic/common, POSIX file/async/thread/event/native-loader and FreeBSD memory sources, with explicit filters. This gives concrete next dependencies for event/thread/file teardown, but their complete bodies and provider backends are not present. Full vendor runtime cannot be inferred from makefile filenames.

The companion hash is a port identity declaration, not independently acquired archive or built binary proof. Per-file integration headers also declare GPLv2-or-later; complete license/distribution applicability is not settled.

Target requires x86_64 and composes many VMM/device/storage/runtime/crypto/TPM libraries. Flags include64bit guests, native NEM, asynchronous completion, shared clipboard, guest control, USB, hardware virtualization and EFI. Common include declares bundled dependency versions and FreeBSD libc headers. These are actual Genode build declarations, not proof every feature is enabled safely in a selected graph, libraries audited, or exact guest CPython/native forms compatible.

The run scenario gives vbox1 RAM3000M/caps1800 but routes VM and default services to parent, GUI/clipboard/report services through other components and optional NIC through a router. It uses ROM/TAR disk inputs, optional RAM overlay, log/RTC/pipe/serial endpoints. The sample Ubuntu_64 guest has RAM2048,two CPUs, writable shared-folder and bidirectional clipboard declarations. These sample numbers/routes are not our frozen closed owner subtree, a total resource bound, or a file/node quota.

GMM uses128MiB RAM slices in a32GiB virtual map, with range-allocator metadata in a libc allocator. New slice attachment loops, requesting8KiB RM RAM or2caps on shortage; other errors free the new dataspace. Pool growth ignores shrink requests; _alloc_pages can grow/recurse after fragmentation. free returns a logical range to the pool, not its RAM dataspace. Fixed map geometry does not bound all VMM/RM/kernel/provider costs, and these retry paths do not contain independent deadlines.

VM allocation creates a page-aligned variable CPU-sized VM structure and a separate SUPPAGE metadata array; CPU records and vCPU registration add ownership. Full upstream destruction and free callsites are not provided by this small wrapper. No absence of a local destructor is promoted to a demonstrated leak; original vendor, support and process/session teardown sources remain necessary.

Emulation threads use dedicated entrypoints,64KiB entrypoint stack plus configured secondary EMT stack, construction signal and blocking completion wait. Factory retains registered entrypoints; other threads delegate to libc pthread creation. The inspected entrypoint destructor body is empty and this file provides no complete bounded pthread join/cancel/drain policy. Member/libc/upstream lifetimes must be traced; no actual hanging or leak was executed.

Startup polls state while Starting with1000ms sleep and no local elapsed/count limit. A PoweredOff event removes capslock ROM/monitors and submits exit; exit reports to parent. This is an event/parent lifecycle, not an independent witness that all guest/device/threads/session/kernel/storage backing is released within a project deadline.

Service integration stores environment access for shared objects. statfs delegates to statvfs but substitutes illustrative nonzero block/free values when underlying fields are zero and warns about bogus shared-folder values; it cannot attest a hard backing quota. README documents GUI sessions and secure-boot/NVRAM configuration, including Windows11 options. Those declarations neither select a guest nor validate exact native artifact forms, side-effect isolation or disk/node lifetime.
